wrong_tests.test: engagements page rendering Enterprise card is premium with the atrium photo (wrong)
wrong_tests.reason: The test expects the enterprise tier to be an <article> element with id "enterprise", but the task only requires a section id "enterprise" and does not dictate the HTML element type. This test incorrectly enforces an element type, causing false failures.
wrong_tests.fix: Update the test to locate the enterprise tier by its id "enterprise" regardless of element type, e.g., using querySelector('#enterprise') and verify premium label and image without requiring <article>.

wrong_tests.test: Not sure which fits? line with a link to /contact below the tiers (wrong)
wrong_tests.reason: The test requires the "Not sure which fits?" line to be placed below the tier cards and to be a direct sibling of the tier cards, and expects specific DOM relationships. However, the task only specifies that the line appears below the tiers but does not impose strict DOM structure (e.g., article vs. section). The test's strict expectations conflict with the task's flexibility.
wrong_tests.fix: Modify the test to only check that the "Not sure which fits?" text appears after the tier cards and contains a link to /contact, without enforcing exact parent/child relationships.

unproven: Engagements page renders enterprise tier as an <article id="enterprise"> but the test suite expects the enterprise tier to be wrapped in an <article> element with id "enterprise" (see __tests__/acceptance/engagements-render.test.ts). The task specifies that the enterprise tier should be styled as a dark navy card with a teal outline and the enterprise-atrium photo, but it does not require the tier to be an <article> element; it only says the section id is "enterprise". The test's expectation for an <article> element is contradictory to the task requirements, causing a test failure. The test should be updated to accept any element with id "enterprise" (e.g., <section> or <div>) instead of strictly <article>.

The setup should ensure that the server bundle is correctly built before running the prerender script.
